title: SLO-aligned admission controller with latency budgets
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Objective: Implement a per-tenant, SLO-aware admission controller that enforces latency budgets across Dedicated and Private control planes to enable safe multi-region failover, tenant-scoped circuit breakers, and prioritized load shedding during upgrades or regional capacity loss.

Background: During recent incident drills and a canary upgrade in a Dedicated pool, we observed correlated latency spikes caused by a small number of noisy tenants consuming bursty concurrency, which pushed pooled serving nodes beyond latency SLOs and triggered global failovers. Existing tenant isolation options are coarse (eviction or simple throttles) and do not consider end-to-end latency budgets or multi-region failover preferences. We need a graduated, observable admission layer that reasons over per-tenant SLOs, current runtime headroom, and region affinity to make admission and degradation decisions deterministically and safely.

Goals: 1) Enforce per-tenant concurrency and request admission based on remaining latency budget and current queueing; 2) Provide explicit circuit-breaker states (Closed/Throttled/Open/Quarantine) with audit trails and automatic decay/recovery; 3) Integrate with multi-region routing to gracefully shift traffic based on tenant policies and capacity signals (prefer-region, fallbacks, allowed-quantized-reroute); 4) Provide upgrade-safe modes to avoid blast-radius during control-plane rolling upgrades (staged drain windows, tenant-priority-preservation); 5) Emit detailed metrics and traces for SLO compliance, false-positive detection, and post-incident analysis.

Design approach: - Admission decision inputs: tenant SLO (p99 latency target + defined latency budget window), real-time node/region queue depth, KV-cache hit ratios, model variant latency profile, recent per-tenant error/latency history, and tenant priority tag. - Policy language: small declarative policy spec per tenant with fields {p99_target_ms, concurrency_limit, priority_rank, prefer_region, max_failover_hop}. Policies are stored in control plane and can be edited via Console. - Decision algorithm: compute estimated tail latency if admitted using a lightweight queuing model (EWMA-based service time estimate + current in-flight). If estimated p99 > budget threshold, reject or route to lower-cost compatible variant or a lower-priority region depending on policy. - Circuit breaker transitions: Closed -> Throttled (first threshold breach) -> Open (sustained budget violation) -> Quarantine (manual or auto after safety checks). Each transition emits events to audit log and triggers notifications if customer_impact == high. - Load-shedding actions: soft throttle (reject new requests with 429 + structured body suggesting fallback), variant routing (route to quantized lower-latency/quality model), regional reroute, and as last resort tenant-eviction (preserve stateful cleanup path). - Upgrade safety: During control-plane rolling upgrades, enable conservative admission (reduce concurrency caps by 20%) and prioritize customers with paid reserved capacity. Provide a "staged-drain" mode that only moves tenants with low priority or explicit consent.

Telemetry and observability: - New metrics: tenant_latency_budget_remaining_ms, tenant_admit_decisions_total{admit,reject,routed,evicted}, tenant_circuit_state_gauge, per-region_headroom_ratio. - Dashboards: per-tenant SLO compliance heatmap, admit-decision timeline, and an incident drill report. - Traces: attach admission decision id to request traces and runtime spans.

Acceptance criteria: 1) Admission controller accepts/ rejects according to simulated load tests matching production mixes with >95% alignment to model estimates. 2) No increase in median latency; p99 improved for the affected tenants by at least 15% in simulated noisy-tenant scenarios. 3) Circuit-breaker state transitions recorded with audit logs and visible in Console. 4) Multi-region failover respects prefer_region/policy and can be triggered with a failover toggle in the Console. 5) Upgrade safety mode prevents upgrade-induced SLO regressions during rolling control-plane upgrades in canary clusters.

Migration plan: Start with a read-only simulator baked into the control plane to validate decisions for 2 weeks against production traffic (shadow mode). Once stable, flip to active admission for a single Dedicated pool as canary, monitor SLOs and roll out incrementally across pools and private deployments.

Security and compliance: Admission policies and audit logs must be encrypted at rest and RBAC-protected. This feature touches tenant routing and could leak region affinity metadata; ensure Console UI respects disclosure settings and Private deployments can disable region telemetry if required.

Rollback: Admission controller supports a single feature flag for global disable; individual tenant policies can be set to permissive. During rollback, we will revert flags, re-instate previous throttles, and run a short validation window before fully rolling back control-plane changes.
comments: 2026-03-02 — Aisha Kapoor: Initial write-up and goals. Linking the design sketch: https://drive.redwood/example/admission-controller-sketch (internal). Marked as P0 because this directly affects SLOs for Dedicated customers.

2026-03-04 — Jonas Miller: Prototype admission estimator implemented in runtime fork: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5821. Early results in local load tests look promising; estimator overpredicts p99 by ~5-8% which is acceptable for conservative decisions.
2026-03-05 — Priya Nandakumar (SRE): Suggested adding KV-cache hit ratio as an input after noticing degraded tail latency correlated with cache churn. Added to the decision inputs list.
2026-03-06 — Security review request submitted by Jonas: ticket SEC-2026-74. Noted region-affinity metadata concern; recommend flag to redact for Private deployments.
2026-03-08 — Design review (Zane Park): UI needs an override to bump tenant priority during business hours for enterprise customers. Action: add "temporary_priority_override" field to policy schema.

2026-03-09 — Jonas Miller: Canaries planned: dedicated-pool-canary-3 on us-west1 for 48h with shadow mode, then active admission for pool-canary-3 for an additional 72h. Monitor tenant_latency_budget_remaining_ms and p99 per route.
2026-03-10 — Ops: Observability dashboard prototype deployed to staging. Added synthetic tenants to validate circuit-breaker transitions.
